dataset: Chilean national electricity grid dataset with hourly power generation data spanning multiple years, capturing the interplay between thermoelectric generation and five renewable and storage energy sources (battery, geothermal, hydroelectric, solar, and wind) in Chile's Sistema Eléctrico Nacional.

short.text: The time series thermoelectric data represents hourly power generation in megawatts (MW) from fossil-fuel-based plants in Chile's national grid, serving as the primary dispatchable generation source to compensate for variability and shortfalls in renewable and storage inputs. This data provides insights into the reliability and stability of the grid, highlighting the importance of thermoelectric power in mitigating the intermittency of renewable energy sources. By analyzing these hourly data points, policymakers and grid operators can optimize energy distribution and ensure a more resilient energy system.

The time series battery represents the hourly power output in megawatts (MW) from grid-scale battery storage systems, capturing the dispatch of previously stored energy to stabilize renewable energy sources and mitigate the residual load on thermoelectric generation. By smoothing out the variability of renewable energy sources, the time series battery helps to reduce the demand on thermoelectric generation, which can be less efficient and more polluting than battery storage. This enables a more efficient and sustainable energy system.

Time series geothermal power generation involves the hourly production of geothermal energy in megawatts (MW), offering a stable and near-baseload renewable source with very low output variability. This predictable contribution reduces the average thermoelectric dispatch requirement throughout the day, as geothermal energy can be reliably integrated into the grid to meet base load demand. By providing a stable and predictable energy source, time series geothermal power generation can help mitigate the variability associated with other renewable energy sources like solar and wind.

Time series hydroelectric power generation in Chile varies seasonally with Andean snowmelt and precipitation cycles, resulting in a strong influence on thermoelectric commitment across seasons. The hourly hydroelectric power generation is a major and partially dispatchable renewable source, meaning it can be controlled to some extent, but its output is still subject to seasonal fluctuations. This variability affects the overall thermoelectric commitment, as hydroelectric power generation can either supplement or reduce the demand for thermoelectric power during different times of the year.

The time series solar represents hourly solar photovoltaic power generation in MW, exhibiting a pronounced midday dip in thermoelectric generation due to its high variability and concentration in daylight hours, followed by a steep ramp-up in the evening. This variability creates fluctuations in thermoelectric generation, which can be mitigated through demand response strategies and energy storage systems. As a result, time series solar data is crucial for optimizing grid operations and managing peak demand.

Time series wind is a variable renewable energy source that generates hourly wind power in megawatts (MW), driven by stochastic fluctuations in meteorological conditions. Its output often anti-correlates with solar power, contributing to offsetting thermoelectric generation, particularly during nighttime and shoulder hours when solar power is typically lower. By complementing solar power, wind energy helps to stabilize thermoelectric generation and reduce the overall variability of the energy mix.
